label: Record store: SQLite or Postgres, and how to reach it

params.name: engine
params.label: Where a domain's records live: sqlite (one file per db, the default) or postgres

params.name: dbs
params.label: With postgres: only these dbs move there (empty = every db) - move one db at a time

params.name: url_env
params.label: The name of the environment variable that holds the Postgres connection string (never the string itself)

params.name: schema_prefix
params.label: Each db is its own Postgres schema, named prefix + db (a prefix lets portals share one database)

params.name: pool_max
params.label: Postgres connections kept open for reuse

params.name: connect_timeout_s
params.label: Seconds to wait for a Postgres connection

params.name: statement_timeout_ms
params.label: Longest one Postgres statement may run (milliseconds)

params.name: sqlite_timeout_s
params.label: Seconds a SQLite save waits for another writer

params.name: pg_types
params.label: Column types the same DDL means on Postgres (SQLite INTEGER is 64-bit)

params.name: sqlite_only
params.label: SQL words that work on SQLite only - a domain module that uses one fails the self-check (write COALESCE, LOWER(col), ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, sqlstore.json_text)

params.name: move_batch
params.label: Rows copied per batch by the move tool

params.name: mysql_url_env
params.label: The environment variable holding a MySQL / MariaDB connection string (mysql scheme: user, password, host, port, database) the move tool reads FROM - never kept in a file

params.name: mysql_types
params.label: MySQL column type -> the Postgres type the move tool creates ("int unsigned" before "int"; {p},{s} = precision, scale). A type not listed stops the move and is named

params.name: words

default.no_url: Set the environment variable {env} to the Postgres connection string first (it is never kept in a file).
default.no_driver: Postgres needs the psycopg package: pip install "psycopg[binary]" (requirements.txt lists it).
default.plan: {db}: {tables} table(s), {rows} row(s) in SQLite -> Postgres schema {schema}.
default.target_busy: Postgres schema {schema} already holds rows ({busy}) - nothing is overwritten. Empty it or pick another schema_prefix.
default.dry: Dry run - nothing written. Add --apply to copy.
default.mismatch: {table}: SQLite {a_rows} row(s) {a_sum}, Postgres {b_rows} row(s) {b_sum} - DIFFERENT, nothing kept
default.done: Moved and checked. Next: set chip store.engine engine = postgres (dbs = ["{db}"] to move only this one) and restart.
default.step_edited: [sqlstore] {db}: migration step {n} was changed after it ran - steps are never edited, add a new one
default.step_failed: {db}: migration step {n} failed and was rolled back - later steps not run: {why}
default.no_mysql_url: Set the environment variable {env} to the MySQL connection string (mysql scheme: user, password, host, port, database) first - it is never kept in a file.
default.no_mysql_driver: Reading MySQL needs the pymysql package: pip install pymysql.
default.mysql_plan: {db}: {tables} table(s), {rows} row(s) in MySQL database {source} -> Postgres schema {schema}.
default.mysql_name: MySQL name {name!r} is not a plain lower-case name - rename it in MySQL first (Postgres would fold its case).
default.mysql_type: {table}.{column}: MySQL type {type!r} has no Postgres type in chip store.engine mysql_types - add one, then move again.
default.mysql_zero_date: {table}.{column}: MySQL holds the zero date '{value}', which no Postgres date can hold - set those rows to NULL in MySQL first.
default.mysql_done: Moved and checked, with keys, indexes and foreign keys. Next: point the portal at Postgres (chip store.engine engine = postgres, {env} set) and restart.

params.label: What the store and its move tool say

description_nl: DomainTemplate 2026-11-11 owner ("start Postgres adapter in DomainTemplate"; AOT benchmark: Postgres + versioned migrations = the #1 gap). core/sqlstore.py reads this chip. engine: sqlite (default - one file per db, exactly as before) or postgres (each db its own schema, prefix + db). dbs: with postgres, only these dbs go there (empty = all) so a portal moves one db at a time. url_env: the NAME of the environment variable holding the connection string - the string and its password are never in a chip or a file. pool_max / connect_timeout_s / statement_timeout_ms / sqlite_timeout_s: connection knobs. pg_types: how the same DDL's column types read on Postgres. sqlite_only: SQL words a domain module may not use (selfcheck 'store'). move_batch: rows per copy batch of python -m core.sqlstore move. words: every line the store and the move tool print.
